## Neuropsychological Assessment

I have extensive experience with neuropsychological assessment in both
clinical and research contexts, including administration,
interpretation, training of others, and adaptation for research
protocols. This spans a broad range of standardised tools, from brief
cognitive screenings to comprehensive neuropsychological batteries, as
well as digital and computerised instruments, symptom validity measures,
and questionnaire-based assessment of mood, fatigue, psychiatric, and
somatic symptoms.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Research Methods & Statistics

**Statistical modelling**\
Inferential statistics; robust statistical modelling; linear and mixed
models; normative modelling; psychometric methods including reliability,
validity, and diagnostic accuracy; network analysis and graphical
modelling; ROC analysis; voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping (VLSM)

**Open science and research design**\
Trial registration; ethics applications (including multi-centre and
industry-collaboration contexts); study protocol development; research data management. 
Completed the [Improving Your Statistical Inferences](https://www.coursera.org/learn/statistical-inferences)
course by Daniël Lakens (Eindhoven University of Technology).

**Data management**\
Large and complex clinical datasets; automated workflow development;
database design and maintenance; data curation and quality control

An ongoing certification programme spanning three tracks: Leadership in

Completed modules:

Some upcoming modules:

**Clinical continuing education**\
Regular participation in internal workshops and lectures covering
various topics, such as dementia, neurodegeneration, stroke, Parkinson's
disease, post-COVID syndrome, fatigue, and subjective cognitive
impairment. Semi-regular participation in departmental
neuropsychological case discussions.

Internal presentations delivered on current and completed research
projects, and e.g., on cultural and linguistic influences on
neuropsychological assessment.

## Networks & Collaboration

**Within the research community**  
Journal club (Cognitive Ageing, Methods, Open Science): Regular participant in a peer-led journal club focusing on
mild cognitive impairment and dementia, methodological topics, open science and reproducibility, neuroimaging, and academic culture.

**Junior Researchers' Lab Meeting**\
Initiated a regular meeting for junior researchers within the lab (independent of senior
faculty) providing a space for research updates, peer support,
coordination, and collaborative problem-solving.

**Clinical and interdisciplinary collaboration**  
Regular collaboration with colleagues from different disciplines, including neurology,
internal medicine, and gynaecology, both within Jena University
Hospital and across partner institutions. Experienced in navigating
the interface between research and clinical care, including coordinating
study procedures within busy clinical departments and contributing to
treatment-relevant research questions.

**Academic networks**  
Active involvement in national and international research collaborations,
with partner institutions and collaborators in Germany, the United
Kingdom, the United States, and Canada. Experienced in coordinating
research across sites, aligning protocols, and maintaining communication
between geographically distributed teams.

**Industry and technology partnerships**  
Substantial experience collaborating with industry partners, including
medical technology companies and start ups. Roles have included serving
as scientific liaison between research teams and software developers,
translating neuropsychological requirements into technical
specifications, and reviewing implementations iteratively to ensure
scientific and clinical integrity throughout the development process.
